SMTO-CMP-0046 — SMTO stopped because repeated steps found nothing new

GUID: 263c2415-e0b6-4c88-943d-ed1af1d5b6b0
Slug: run-no-new-information
Domain: CMP · Subsystem: cmp

What happened

  • SMTO tried three steps in a row that turned up nothing new, so it stopped instead of looping. What you asked for isn't confirmed yet, but the work and results so far are kept.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Open the last few steps under this task and read what each one returned. They show what SMTO kept checking and why it couldn't get any further.
  2. Send a new message with what was missing, such as the exact, current file, folder, computer or name to use, or describe a different way to do it. SMTO stopped because the same checks kept giving the same answers; new details give it something different to try.
  3. If something changed since you asked, for example a file was renamed or moved, give SMTO the new name or location. Out-of-date names are a common reason repeated steps find nothing.

What success looks like

  • SMTO's next steps return new results and the task ends as Completed instead of Partial.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them, with what you asked SMTO to do, to the person who manages SMTO. Don't turn off Stop non-progressing loops in Agent Checks to get past this; it would let SMTO loop without making progress.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • The run stopped as partial because the no-information guard saw three consecutive operations return no new information, leaving the requested outcome unconfirmed.

What this means

  • The enabled no-information guard observes a no_information_streak of at least three and stops further unproductive repetition. Completion checks consume retained evidence and the effective guard policy; they do not execute work. A rejected declaration preserves the answer and successful receipts, and only the original operation evidence establishes effects.

Why this can happen

  • The enabled no-information guard observes a no_information_streak of at least three and stops further unproductive repetition.

How to diagnose it

  • Inspect the last receipts and unresolved requirement to identify a genuinely different next step.

How to fix it

  • Review the last three operation results and the open requirement in the run's activity to see why each call returned nothing new (wrong or outdated target, missing input, unavailable resource). Resume or re-prompt with a corrected approach or new input; keep the progress.no_information_stop guard ('Stop non-progressing loops') enabled.
  • Inspect the last receipts and unresolved requirement. Continue only with a corrected approach or new evidence, preserving prior successful work.

Retry and execution caution

  • Correct the recorded cause, then inspect current state and existing receipts before requesting another attempt.

How to verify the fix

  • Any continuation adds relevant new evidence or corrects the actual approach without replaying known effects.

What not to do

  • Do not submit a stale identifier or revision after another actor changed the resource.

Technical notes

  • Completion checks consume retained evidence and the effective guard policy; they do not execute work. A rejected declaration preserves the answer and successful receipts, and only the original operation evidence establishes effects.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
